articles.title: eMudhra CA Key Compromise: A Technical Postmortem (2026)
articles.excerpt: Summary On October 17, 2026, an independent researcher (credited as “Wayne”) proved to Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla and eMudhra that he held the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA cert…
articles.body: Summary On October 17, 2026 , an independent researcher (credited as “Wayne”) proved to Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla and eMudhra that he held the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates . Six were TLS issuing CAs trusted by every major browser; two were code-signing CAs trusted by Microsoft. Nobody had stolen anything. The keys were ECDSA P-384 private scalars smaller than 256 : effectively one byte of entropy instead of 384 bits. One key was literally the number 4 ; the others were 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237. Anyone could recover them from the public certificates in milliseconds, and AI agents did it from a one-line prompt. The keys had been sitting in publicly trusted, cross-signed, audited certificates since April 30, 2025 , about 18 months.

articles.title: Is a Trading Bot Worth It? An Honest Way to Decide
articles.excerpt: Is a trading bot worth it? Only if its edge survives fees, slippage, funding costs and your own ability to leave it running through a drawdown, and most bots never get tested well enough to show that.…
articles.body: Is a trading bot worth it? Only if its edge survives fees, slippage, funding costs and your own ability to leave it running through a drawdown, and most bots never get tested well enough to show that. A bot is worth considering when it has a long, honest test record and a risk you can tolerate. It is not worth it because of a screenshot or a win rate. This guide gives you a way to decide for yourself, with a worked example and a checklist you can apply to any bot, including ones you build. Is a trading bot worth it? Start with what you are paying "Worth it" means the bot's net result beats what it costs you, adjusted for risk. The costs are more than a subscription: Trading fees. Every entry and exit pays a fee, and frequent traders pay it hundreds of times a month. Slippage.

articles.title: Ctrl+F Works in Your PDF Viewer Until Someone Searches a Scanned Contract
articles.excerpt: You add search to your PDF viewer. You type a word from the first page and it highlights correctly. Everything looks done. Then a user searches a scanned contract and gets zero results. Another search…
articles.body: You add search to your PDF viewer. You type a word from the first page and it highlights correctly. Everything looks done. Then a user searches a scanned contract and gets zero results. Another searches for “office” and misses every match, because the document stores the “ffi” as a single ligature character. PDF search looks simple but depends on how the text was stored. Why PDF text is awkward A PDF does not store a paragraph. It stores positioned fragments of text. A single line may be split into several pieces, words can break across fragments, and the order in the file may not match the reading order. Detect pages with no text at all A scanned PDF is often just images. There is no text to search, so extraction returns nothing.

articles.body: Part 3 of a series on Movie Engine, where an AI agent edits Kdenlive video projects while the editor stays open. Earlier: Part 1, the overview , Part 2, UI Automation without stealing focus . Movie Engine makes a running Kdenlive reload a project by pressing File > Revert through Windows UI Automation. UI Automation finds controls by their name , and the name is whatever the interface shows. In English it is "File" and "Revert". In German it is "Datei" and "Zuletzt gespeicherte Fassung". In Japanese it is "ファイル(F)" and "戻す(V)". The launchers start Kdenlive in English by default ( LANGUAGE=en_US ), but a user who prefers their own language sets MOVIE_ENGINE_UI_LANG=de and the automation must still work. This post is about where the names come from and how each language is checked.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. articles.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
articles.excerpt: The longest total solar eclipse on land this century promises to be the experience of a lifetime, but watching it from Luxor, Egypt, may not be straightforward. What could go wrong? Quite a lot, actua…
articles.body: On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part.
articles.author: Jamie Carter
